title: M&I/Partners is an influence route into Dutch healthcare, not a delivery partner
content:
The flag on M&I/Partners is unambiguous: not a delivery partner. It directs the firm to be routed to the healthcare vertical via influence instead, and cites one concrete artefact as the reason — it benchmarks hospital IT spend at 6.0% of revenue.

The mechanism is its vendor-neutrality, which the record describes as by design rather than incidental. A firm that never carries a build has no platform slot to win and no bench to staff, so it cannot be scored the way an integrator is. What it produces instead is analysis that healthcare buyers use, and a published spend benchmark is the kind of output that a whole sector reads. That is why the research treats it as leverage rather than as pipeline.

Two caveats bound the claim. The row is a provisional v2 tail entry, rescored mechanically on size and slot occupancy with no v3 evidence, so this is a hypothesis about a channel rather than a qualified relationship. And the priority field still carries an outstanding OSS-portfolio screen, which for an advisory firm is a cheaper check than for a delivery house.
